title: Enzyme-substrate complex model
body: The model showing that an enzyme-mediated reaction occurs only when the shape and charge of the substrate are compatible with the enzyme's active site.
caution: State both shape and charge compatibility with the active site, not shape alone.
ced_evidence: 3.1.A.2 — "the shape and charge of the substrate must be compatible with the active site of the enzyme"

title: Domains sharing conserved core metabolic pathways
body: Core metabolic pathways such as glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation are conserved across all currently recognized domains, which supports common ancestry.

items.label: Archaea
items.meaning: Domain in which the core metabolic pathways are conserved

items.label: Bacteria
items.meaning: Domain in which the core metabolic pathways are conserved

items.label: Eukarya
items.meaning: Domain in which the core metabolic pathways are conserved

ced_evidence: 3.3.B.1 — "conserved across all currently recognized domains (Archaea, Bacteria, and Eukarya)"

title: Metabolic pathway (sequential energy pathway)
body: An energy-related pathway in which reactions occur in sequence so that energy is transferred in a controlled way, and a product of one reaction is typically the reactant for the next step.
ced_evidence: 3.3.A.3 — "A product of a reaction in a metabolic pathway is typically the reactant for the subsequent step in the pathway."

title: Aerobic cellular respiration in eukaryotes: order of stages
body: Order in which aerobic respiration captures energy from glucose in a eukaryotic cell, from glycolysis through oxidative phosphorylation.

items.label: 1. Glycolysis (cytosol)
items.meaning: Releases energy in glucose to form ATP, NADH (from NAD+), and pyruvate

items.label: 2. Pyruvate transport and oxidation
items.meaning: Pyruvate moves from the cytosol to the mitochondrion, where oxidation occurs

items.label: 3. Krebs (citric acid) cycle (mitochondrial matrix)
items.meaning: Releases CO2, synthesizes ATP, and reduces NAD+ to NADH and FAD to FADH2

items.label: 4. Electron transport chain (inner mitochondrial membrane)
items.meaning: NADH and FADH2 deliver electrons that pass through the ETC to oxygen, the terminal electron acceptor, and a proton gradient forms

items.label: 5. Oxidative phosphorylation
items.meaning: Protons flow back through ATP synthase by chemiosmosis, driving ATP formation from ADP and inorganic phosphate

ced_evidence: 3.5.B.1–3.5.B.5, 3.5.A.3 — "Electrons extracted in glycolysis and Krebs cycle reactions are transferred by NADH and FADH2 to the ETC"

title: Required components of a constructed graph
body: Components a graph must include when constructing it to represent data.

items.label: Type of graph
items.meaning: Appropriate for the data (x-y graphs such as bar, histogram, line, log scale, dual y; scatter plot; box and whisker plot; pie chart)

items.label: Axis labeling
items.meaning: Axes labeled with appropriate units, plus a legend

items.label: Accurately plotted data
items.meaning: Data points plotted accurately, including error bars when appropriate

ced_evidence: Skill 4.A — "The graph should include the following components"
